Video of id Software's Super Mario Bros. 3 Demo (1990)

This was a demo that John Carmack, and John Romero created, while still working at Softdisk, that demonstrated smooth side scrolling (using adaptive tile refresh, invented by Carmack) in an IBM compatible PC game, which hadn't been achieved before that time. They approached Nintendo with the demo, I guess hoping to make Super Mario Bros. 3 for the PC, but Nintendo wasn't interested in the PC market at the time, and declined.

However, this side scrolling breakthrough led to John Carmack, John Romero, Tom Hall, and Adrian Carmack forming id, and the creation of the Commander Keen series, which was the beginning of their success.

I had heard/read of this demo before, and always wondered what it actually looked/played like. Awesome to finally see some video of it. It's actually much better than I expected. Note the Commander Keen sound effects in the demo. Funny to see Mario with Keen sounds.

As a side note, if anyone is interested in id Software's history/gaming history, I suggest checking out the book Masters of Doom. It's pretty good.
